clue.text: Challenging attitude of Spanish husband-to be

parts.note: de is the Spanish word for 'of'
a fiancé is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A Spanish bridegroom-to-be strikes a confrontational pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance, a stance that challenges authority.

clue.text: Declines to swallow large amounts of drink about noon

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the drink word goes round a letter

parts.note: swigs are big gulps of drink

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to knock back big gulps around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' reads as a verb meaning refuses, but it is a plural noun; 'about' is the container signal, putting the noon letter inside the gulps of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Downswings are downturns, periods when figures decline.

clue.text: Hurried to secure job putting up adverts

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: flying means hurried, as in a flying visit
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off to land work pasting up posters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To secure' is the container signal: the job is held inside the word for hurried. Flyposting is illegal bill-sticking, a familiar British term.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyposting is sticking bills on walls or hoardings without permission.

clue.text: Make amends together

explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make up for a wrong; 'at one' means united or in agreement.

clue.text: Invader opposed to dispersing riot squad

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: dispersing a crowd scatters it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invader objects to the police breaking up a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispersing' is the anagram signal on 'riot squad'; the surface's police unit is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquistador was a Spanish conqueror of the Americas, an invader.

clue.text: Rogues given temporary shelter on board ship

indicators.note: something on board a ship sits between its letters, as cargo sits inside a vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a camp is a temporary place of shelter

explanation.surface: Villains are offered a makeshift refuge aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the container signal, taken from the crossword habit of putting a word between the two letters of SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamps are mischievous rascals, a mild word for rogues.

clue.text: Revolutionary on the wagon achieving gymnastic feat?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' and 'on the wagon' suggest a teetotal radical, but the first definition is a wheel turning on a cart; 'achieving' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart's wheel revolves; a cartwheel is also a sideways handspring.

clue.text: Proper gathering

explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old word for fitting; a meet is also an assembly, as of hunters.

clue.text: Girl with antique display?

parts.note: she stands for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A young woman shows off an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antique' is an adjective on the definition: shew is the archaic spelling of show.
explanation.definitionFit: Shew is an archaic spelling of show, a verb meaning display.

clue.text: Wait — pony's drooping: find somewhere to stop

indicators.note: something drooping has sagged out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive gives no letter; the word pony is fodder

explanation.surface: A rider tells a flagging horse to hold on while looking for a rest stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drooping' rearranges WAIT and PONY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A waypoint is a stopping place or marked point on a planned route.

clue.text: Don't move wall decoration, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals a word heard rather than read, so its sound counts

parts.note: a frieze is a decorated band running along a wall

explanation.surface: Someone is warned to stand still beside an ornamental wall panel.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to stop dead and stay motionless, as ordered by a sentry.

clue.text: Flight lieutenant has unusual type of rifle for battle

parts.note: Fl is short for Flight Lieutenant, an RAF rank
odd means unusual
the Enfield is a British military rifle

explanation.surface: An RAF officer carries an odd rifle into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Flodden Field (1513) in Northumberland saw the English defeat James IV of Scotland; 'has' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Flodden Field was a 1513 clash where James IV of Scotland died.

clue.text: Bird flying about in US owl centre

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird circles over an American owl sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying about' rearranges US, OWL and CENTRE; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone curlew is a long-legged wading bird of dry heaths.

clue.text: Flatmate, perhaps, ruined coat in bath

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's housemate spoiled a coat by leaving it in the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohabitant lives with another; a flatmate is one example.

clue.text: Top card player's

parts.note: read as the head of a group playing a well-known card game, with 's as 'is'

explanation.surface: A champion card player is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer really means a forward military position; the clue reads it as the leading player of a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a forward position seized in enemy territory; literally, a head of bridge players.

clue.text: Popular group mislaying one piece of music, initially

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: mislaying means losing something, so a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a trio is a group of three musicians
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A popular band loses a member before their first number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mislaying' takes I out of TRIO, leaving TRO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a song, what plays at the start.

clue.text: Cracks an individual's noticed, when going round ship

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: one's is the possessive of one, an individual
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone's jokes get attention on a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' is the container signal: the possessive of 'one' encloses the ship. 'Noticed' adds nothing to the wordplay and serves the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracks are witty quips, the same as short jokes or wisecracks.

clue.text: Southern border secure after battle

parts.note: an edge is a border or margin
to moor a boat is to secure it

explanation.surface: After a battle, the southern frontier is made safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Sedgemoor in Somerset, England, was the last pitched battle on English soil (1685); 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedgemoor names the 1685 clash ending Monmouth's rebellion against James II.

clue.text: Drink a soldier's served to general in mess?

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: in a mess means jumbled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A private carries a drink to a general in the mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like the officers' dining room but is the anagram signal on GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: Story teller finally paid a 6 bit of money, once

parts.note: a liar tells stories, untrue ones

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word paid

explanation.surface: A storyteller ends up paying a small sum in old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The liard was a small copper coin of old France, now obsolete.

clue.text: Rather pleasant, being in charge

parts.note: an offensive is a military charge or attack

explanation.surface: Someone in authority turns out to be quite agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like 'in command' but is read as IN plus OFFENSIVE (an attack).
explanation.definitionFit: Inoffensive means harmless and unobjectionable, so mildly agreeable.

clue.text: Kingdom of fine palaces

indicators.note: of means made out of, so the answer is formed from letters within the words

explanation.surface: A realm known for its elegant royal residences.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal was a Himalayan kingdom until it became a republic in 2008.

clue.text: Release without charge

explanation.definitionFit: To free is to let go; free also means costing nothing.

clue.text: Refuse to pack up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly

explanation.surface: Someone declines to pack their bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun: marc is the residue of pressed grapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the leftover skins and pips after grapes are pressed, a kind of waste.

clue.text: Blocking the way, soldiers made a loud noise

indicators.note: blocking a road means standing in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a road is a way
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops barricading a road bellowed loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blocking' is the container signal: the soldiers stand in the middle of the way, cutting it open after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Roared means bellowed or thundered, making a great din.

clue.text: His Excellency the Prime Minister, introduced by former friend

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: introduced by means taken into the following word, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: An ambassador and the premier are introduced by an old pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced by' is the container signal: the premier's initials go inside 'former' (late, as in the late king), and the ambassador's title comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is a companion and helper, especially a spouse.

clue.text: Former tax surplus

parts.note: ex- means former
a cess is a tax or levy

explanation.surface: An old levy produced a surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess is an amount over and above what is needed.

clue.text: Admired article penned by mature journalist

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within the following word, as in a pen

parts.note: adult means mature, fully grown
a is the indefinite article
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A seasoned reporter wrote a piece that was much praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing but means enclosed: A goes inside ADULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulated means praised to excess, worshipped and admired.
